text:
ACME SRE: hey, production incident — multiple customers reported streaming responses stuck on client reconnect. after the client reconnects we sometimes see partial output, then a 401 and the client hangs. also billing shows duplicate token usage for some of those requests :/
ACME SRE: repro: ts sdk, using our reconnect wrapper over EventSource. if token expires between disconnect and reconnect, reconnect attempt returns 401 but the client still prints a few more chunks then stops. billing shows two requests counted.
ACME SRE: attaching logs + tiny repro below. high priority — customer on Dedicated, hitting this in prod.
jessica: thanks — assigning. can you paste the minimal repro and logs here? any correlation id from the server logs?
ACME SRE: no correlation id in the payload we got, but the request-id header was: req-9f3b. logs: 
```
[2026-02-18T14:02:03Z] client: starting stream, token expires in 2s
[2026-02-18T14:02:05Z] client: stream disconnected (network) -> reconnecting
[2026-02-18T14:02:05Z] client: re-opened stream, received chunk: 'partial A'
[2026-02-18T14:02:06Z] server: auth failed: token expired -> 401
[2026-02-18T14:02:06Z] client: received chunk: 'partial B' then no more, iterator never resolves
[2026-02-18T14:02:07Z] billing: two events recorded for req-9f3b
```
ACME SRE: minimal TS repro below (uses EventSource polyfill, wrapper tries to auto-reconnect + heartbeat, cancels on close):
```ts
import EventSource from 'eventsource'
async function streamWithReconnect(url, token) {
  let abort = false
  let es
  while (!abort) {
    es = new EventSource(url + '?t=' + Date.now(), { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } })
    es.onmessage = e => console.log('CHUNK', e.data)
    es.onerror = e => {
      console.log('ES ERR', e)
      es.close()
      // backoff
    }
    // heartbeat to keep connection alive
    const hb = setInterval(() => es.dispatchEvent(new MessageEvent('heartbeat')), 15000)
    await new Promise((res) => es.addEventListener('close', res))
    clearInterval(hb)
    // token may refresh externally between loops
  }
}
```
jessica: cool, this is very helpful. initial guess: client-side reconnect can race with server-side auth expiry, and our runtime may emit residual chunks from the old connection while the reconnect path is tearing down, which can look like duplicate output. the billing double-count could be because the old connection is not flagged as aborted at the accounting layer. tagging eng-runtime. @amar can you take a look?
amar: looking. thanks for the repro, nice and small. quick note: we've seen a similar pattern when using continuous batching + early auth failure — old KV cache entries cause leftover send events. two hypotheses: 1) event emitter not unregistered on reconnect (JS side) so handler gets attached twice; 2) server accepts reconnect long enough to stream a few chunks before rejecting auth and the accounting treats both as separate completed "requests". will instrument.
li-yuan: on the runtime side i can confirm we recently changed the auth check order to be slightly later to reduce cold-start latency for token verification when there is a cached connection. that could cause a few chunks to emit before the check fails. i'll revert the ordering for the next canary and add a strict check for token validity before any chunk is emitted.
nina: also saw reports from Python SDK customers hitting a hang when the async iterator never raises after a reconnect 401. likely the iterator's internal queue isn't being closed on error. i'll open a quick fix to ensure iterator errors propagate.
jessica: action items:
- eng-runtime (li-yuan): add pre-auth gate and ensure no chunks emitted after auth failure; add a server-side correlation id header for all stream chunks.
- devex (amar): add a safety unregister in TS SDK reconnect path so onmessage handlers are removed before reattach; ensure AbortController abort tears down EventSource immediately.
- SDKs (nina): patch Python async iterator to propagate errors and close the iterator when server sends 401 on reconnect. check Go/Java too.
- support (jessica): gather list of impacted accounts and confirm billing duplicates, offer temporary credits if confirmed.
amar: quick interim workaround for customers: refresh token proactively 5s before expiry and short-circuit reconnect if Auth returns non-2xx; also dedupe chunks by sequence id on client side if you can.
ACME SRE: thanks — can you also share a short mitigation we can deploy in our client now while you patch? they prefer a client-only fix.
amar: pasteable client mitigation (TS):
```ts
// naive dedupe wrapper for EventSource chunks
const seen = new Set()
es.onmessage = e => {
  const id = JSON.parse(e.data).seq || e.lastEventId
  if (seen.has(id)) return
  seen.add(id)
  console.log('CHUNK', e.data)
}
// call es.close() and remove handlers before reconnecting
es.onmessage = null
es.onerror = null
es.close()
```
li-yuan: i pushed a runtime canary that changes auth ordering + correlation id in headers. canary id: canary/stream-auth-2026-02-18. please repro there: https://canary.example.internal/streams. note: this will block chunk emission if the token is expired at connection time.
sre-bot: deploy canary/stream-auth-2026-02-18 completed to canary cluster (ok:3 failed:0) — links: https://ci.example/build/9876
ACME SRE: testing canary now... reproduces less often but still saw one case where two chunks arrived before 401. attaching new logs.
```
[2026-02-18T14:22:01Z] client: reconnect attempt
[2026-02-18T14:22:01Z] server(canary): accepted connection, sent chunk 'x'
[2026-02-18T14:22:01Z] server(canary): auth check failed -> 401, closing
[2026-02-18T14:22:01Z] client: got 'x', 'y' then hang
```
amar: that log is interesting — server sent two chunks before final close. i'll instrument the kernel to not flush any buffered chunks once auth is known to fail. could be batching flusher running after the auth check but before close.
li-yuan: agreed. i found a code path in continuous batching where flush is scheduled regardless of auth state; patching to cancel pending flush tasks when auth fails. i'll roll a patch to canary in ~30m.
jessica: great. nina, any ETA for the Python sdk iterator patch?
nina: small change — will open PR in 1h, publish patch to pip in the next release cycle, and cut an emergency release if customers need it sooner.
ACME SRE: appreciate the quick turnaround. can you add billing team to the thread for duplicate-charge investigation? we can provide request-ids.
jessica: adding billing and cc'ing the account owner. we will follow up on credits if duplicate charges confirmed.
li-yuan: patch pushed to canary, new canary id canary/stream-auth-2026-02-18-v2. please retest. i also added a header X-Req-Correlation to every chunk, should make debugging easier.
sre-bot: canary/stream-auth-2026-02-18-v2 deployed (ok:4 failed:0) — https://ci.example/build/9881
ACME SRE: retested — looks clean now, no duplicate chunks and iterator resolves with 401 error. billing team confirmed only one usage event for the test req-9f3b.
jessica: marking as triaged. follow-ups: backport runtime fix to prod, release SDK patches (TS safety unregister + Python iterator), and billing writeup. will create a postmortem and share with the account. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
amar: i've also started a short doc for DevEx with sample mitigation code and gotchas for reconnect + auth, will share link when ready.
ACME SRE: thanks all, appreciate the quick fix.
